chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: To do any kind of analysis on the data, we need significant amount of data.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: So let's read data for each stock for a period of one year, that is year 2010.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: You can do this by changing the start and the end date as shown here.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: Let's see the data frame content now.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: So this is your data frame which has stock prices for

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: the symbol SPY, Google, IBM and Gold for a year 2010.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: We briefly explained you slicing in the last lesson.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: In this lesson, we will learn how to do slicing using the data frame we just created.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: There are basically three way we can slice the data frame.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: First, row slicing.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: As the name suggests, it will give us the required rows along with all the columns.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: This is useful when you want to compare movement of all the stocks over a subset of time.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: This is how you do it in the code.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: We use the function dot ix of the data frame and

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: just mention the start and the end date in the square brackets.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: Here we extract the movement of all the stocks in the month of Jan.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: Note that the start and the end date should be in the chronological order.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: If you write the 31st Jan date before 1st Jan,

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: the data frame will give you an empty data frame.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: Even if you remove the dot ix function and just try to print df passing the dates

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: in the chronological order, you will get the same result.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: However, dot ix is considered to be more pythonic and robust.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: So we follow that.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: Now let's run the code to see the stock prices for the month of January.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: You can observe that we get the data only for the January month, but for all the symbols.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: This is known as row slicing.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: Second way of slicing is useful when you want to view prices of only one stock over the date range.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: In this case, you can use column slicing.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: We want to project the prices of Google for the entire year of 2010.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: Here is how we do it.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: A square bracket along with the name of the column, and do not forget the colon.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: To retrieve a single column, we just pass a single label.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: To select multiple columns, we pass a list of labels.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: Let's print this.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: And this is the output for multiple columns.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: The last way of slicing is to slice through both dimension.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: That is rows and columns.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: The most robust way to do this is using the ix selector of the data frame.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: Let's go ahead and use it.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: If you need more than one column, you define them in a list like this.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: And date range are separated with a colon.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: Here you go.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: The stock prices for the symbol SPY and IBM over the date range, 10th March to 15th March.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: One application of this way of slicing is to compare multiple stocks over a period of time.

chunks.title: More slicing
chunks.text: Pandas support many ways of slicing a data frame to suit different needs.
